About the Lab

Five ways to look at the same bridge.

Nexus Lab is a civil engineering research group working across structures, transportation, and the cities they serve — from Dhaka to Miami. Our name is also our method: five connected lines of inquiry that treat infrastructure as one continuous system, not five separate problems.

NNetworks EEngineering XeXploration UUrban Systems SStructures
Research Focus

What NEXUS stands for, in practice.

Each pillar is a real line of active work in the lab — not a category we made up for the acronym.

N
Networks

Transportation network resilience

Modeling mobility networks under stress — from V2X-enabled e-scooter and mixed-traffic simulations in CARLA and SUMO, to folding network efficiency directly into how bridge repairs get prioritized.

E
Engineering

Structural & seismic engineering

Nonlinear finite element analysis in Abaqus, CFRP/FRP strengthening of reinforced concrete beam-column joints under cyclic loading, and QA/QC on live infrastructure megaprojects.

X
eXploration

Multi-hazard risk & digital twins

GIS-based coastal exposure and flood-risk workflows spanning multiple U.S. states, hurricane-driven rain intrusion studies, and digital twin frameworks that fuse hazard data with building performance.

U
Urban Systems

Equity-focused infrastructure

Decision-support frameworks that link hazard intensity, structural condition, and community accessibility — plus research into socioeconomic mobility and post-pandemic urban travel patterns.

S
Structures

Bridge rehabilitation prioritization

Mining multi-state National Bridge Inventory data to build interpretable frameworks for deciding what gets rehabilitated first — and defending why.

Who's in the Lab

Two countries, one lab.

Led from Florida International University, with researchers based in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and mentorship support reaching toward El Paso, Texas — Nexus Lab is small by design and collaborative by necessity.

Mostafa Sameer, M.Sc.
HEAD INVESTIGATOR & PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR
Ph.D. Candidate, Civil Engineering — Florida International University

Mostafa leads Nexus Lab's work on bridge infrastructure analytics and rehabilitation prioritization, drawing on multi-state National Bridge Inventory data from Florida, Texas, Pennsylvania, California, and New York. His research also spans GIS-based coastal exposure and flood-risk modeling, multi-hazard analysis, and digital twin frameworks for resilient infrastructure decisions. He holds an M.Sc. in Transportation Engineering from Wayne State University and a B.Sc. in Civil Engineering from Ahsanullah University of Science & Technology (AUST).

Utsho Kundu
Graduate Assistant to the PI
Civil Engineering Graduate, AUST — Structural Engineering, 2022–2026

Utsho's work centers on structural and seismic engineering — reinforced concrete behavior, FRP strengthening, and nonlinear finite element analysis in Abaqus. His undergraduate thesis examined RC beam-column joints strengthened with CFRP under cyclic loading, and he contributes to the lab through numerical modeling, literature review, and data analysis.

Sheikh Md. Iftakhar Uddin
Graduate Assistant to the PI
Graduate Student, Civil Engineering, AUST — Environmental Engineering

Iftakhar works at the intersection of environmental and transportation engineering — urban sustainability, air pollution and environmental quality, resilient infrastructure, GIS & spatial analysis, remote sensing, and AI/ML in civil engineering. His undergraduate thesis designed a bio-filter for removing Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) from the gaseous phase. At Nexus Lab, he contributes through GIS-based spatial analysis, remote sensing & satellite data processing, and AI/ML modeling.

Environmental Eng. GIS & Remote Sensing AI/ML
Guest Speaker & Student Mentor
Md Ali Ahnaf Abid Mayukh
CIVIL & ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEER
Support Wing — Guest Speaker & Student Mentor, Nexus Lab

Mayukh is a Civil and Environmental Engineer with a B.Sc. from the Islamic University of Technology (IUT), specializing in geospatial infrastructure design, remote sensing, and environmental analysis. He serves as an Outside Plant (OSP) Engineer at SKARION Engineering Services Ltd., designing large-scale fiber optic routes and XGS-PON telecommunications networks across key U.S. markets, preparing municipal and utility permit packages, and mentoring junior designers. His broader profile bridges advanced spatial modeling — using ArcGIS Pro and Google Earth Engine for environmental hazard mapping — with corporate training experience as an AutoCAD Instructor at LEAD Academy and a Certified Supply Chain Analyst (CSCA) from ISCEA. At Nexus Lab, he joins the support wing as a guest speaker and mentor, sharing industry experience and guiding students through their research journey.

Upcoming at Nexus Lab

A guest session with Mayukh.

GuestTalk

Guest Speaker & Mentorship Session — Md Ali Ahnaf Abid Mayukh

Mayukh is joining Nexus Lab's support wing as a guest speaker and student mentor, sharing his industry experience in geospatial infrastructure design, fiber network engineering, and remote sensing — and guiding lab students through their own research journeys.

We're also excited to share that Mayukh will be joining the University of Texas at El Paso (UTEP) as a Graduate Research Assistant (GRA) in Spring 2027, continuing his academic and research journey at a university recognized for its strong research focus and commitment to its binational community.
